questions.question_text: According to the chapter, why is preparing for questions important for a speaker?

options.text: It ensures the audience won’t ask any questions
It helps anticipate audience queries and practice thoughtful responses, boosting credibility and calmness
It allows the speaker to avoid answering difficult questions
It is only necessary for professional speakers, not studentsCorrect Answer:B. It helps anticipate audience queries and practice thoughtful responses, boosting credibility and calmness

questions.question_text: What is a key component of active listening skills as described in the chapter?

options.text: Thinking about your response while the other person is speaking
Fully focusing on and understanding the question before answering, showing respect through attention and body language
Interrupting to answer quickly and show confidence
Looking at notes or the audience instead of the askerCorrect Answer:B. Fully focusing on and understanding the question before answering, showing respect through attention and body language

questions.question_text: How does the chapter suggest responding with confidence to a tough or unexpected question?

options.text: Immediately say “I don’t know” and move on
Pause briefly, stay calm, use a confident tone, and structure a short, clear answer even if unsure
Avoid answering by changing the topic
Speak as quickly as possible to hide uncertaintyCorrect Answer:B. Pause briefly, stay calm, use a confident tone, and structure a short, clear answer even if unsure

questions.question_text: What does the chapter recommend for accepting and using feedback effectively?

options.text: Ignore criticism and focus only on positive comments
Listen without defending, ask for specifics, and apply actionable points to improve skills
Argue with the person giving feedback to clarify your intent
Avoid seeking feedback to prevent hearing negative commentsCorrect Answer:B. Listen without defending, ask for specifics, and apply actionable points to improve skills

questions.question_text: What is a common challenge teens face when handling feedback, as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: Always receiving too much positive feedback, making it hard to improve
Feeling embarrassed or defensive about criticism, often brushing it off instead of using it for growth
Never receiving feedback because they don’t ask for it
Finding feedback too easy to apply without effortCorrect Answer:B. Feeling embarrassed or defensive about criticism, often brushing it off instead of using it for growth
